extracted.intended_audience: students of literature, aspiring fiction writers, and literary scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and apply Henry James’s principles from 'The Art of Fiction' to evaluate or guide the writing of novels and literary fiction—emphasizing artistic freedom, realism grounded in experience, point of view, and showing vs telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction as a serious art form
rubrics_metrics.description: “The only reason for the existence of a novel is that it does attempt to represent life.” Novels should be judged by artistic standards, not merely moral ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fiction by aesthetic and representational merits—craft, depth, and capacity to represent life—rather than by whether it provides moral instruction or entertainment. The novel can capture human experience with unique psychological depth and deserves the same respect as painting, music, or poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of the artist / rejection of prescriptive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: James rejected Besant’s proposed specific “laws” for novelists and argued that there are no essential “rules” for writing fiction: "The execution belongs to the author alone; it is what is most personal to him, and we measure him by that."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize authorial freedom and experimentation with structure, technique, and subject matter. Treat prescriptive formulas and moral constraints as anti-patterns; the only true test is whether the work succeeds on its own terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary obligation: the work must be interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: James’s claim that “the only obligation to which we may hold a novel… is that it be interesting.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'interestingness'—engagement, perceptive observation, and aesthetic vitality—as a core evaluative standard. A work need not conform to external moral rules if it compellingly represents life or consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience as the foundation of fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experience is never limited... an immense sensibility... catching every air-borne particle in its tissue.” For James, the writer’s experience forms the raw material of fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well the author filters and processes observation and personal perception into fiction. Reward keen observation, subtle processing of lived experience, and the use of the writer’s sensibility as a productive source rather than rote invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism / 'air of reality' (solidity of specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The air of reality (solidity of specification) seems to me to be the supreme virtue of a novel.” Realism involves psychological complexity, attention to nuance and detail, and authenticity that makes characters feel alive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value specificity, detailed rendering, and internal plausibility. Check for concrete sensory detail, credible psychology, and nuanced depiction that create the impression characters 'live beyond the page.' Avoid contrivance and generic flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological depth and complex characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed exploration of characters’ thoughts, feelings, and motivations; moral and psychological ambiguity; characters shaped by social contexts but with rich inner lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge characterization by subtle shifts in perception and internal development rather than by plot exposition alone. Reward ambiguity, internal conflict, and characters whose interiority affects action and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view and perspective (central consciousness and limited POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques include the “central consciousness” where events are filtered through a character’s perception, limited point of view creating ambiguity, multiple perspectives for layered understanding, and unreliable narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how POV choices shape meaning: whether a central consciousness yields psychological insight, whether limited POV invites reader interpretation, and whether multiple or unreliable perspectives are used to complicate truth. Assess consistency and how well POV serves the work’s aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing versus telling (dramatic presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: James advocated revealing character through action and dialogue, avoiding direct authorial commentary, creating scenes that reveal information gradually, and trusting readers to draw conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer scenes that dramatize rather than summarize. Penalize heavy-handed authorial exposition or explicit moralizing. Reward use of action, dialogue, and scene construction that allow readers to infer character and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter freedom: no prescribed limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: James maintained that subject matter should not be limited by convention or morality and that "all experience is valid material."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reject a work solely for controversial or unconventional subject matter; instead evaluate how the material is handled artistically and whether it contributes to the novel’s representation of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic success judged on its own terms (not moral clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment criteria should focus on artistic success rather than moral clarity or adherence to rules—contrast to Besant’s emphasis on moral instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing or teaching, foreground internal coherence, craft, and representational achievement. Avoid conflating ethical positions of characters or provoked discomfort with aesthetic failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques: attention to nuance, detail, and subtlety
rubrics_metrics.description: James’s writing emphasizes nuance, fine specification, and gradual revelation—small details and subtle shifts of perception are central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the writer’s control of tone, texture, and small-scale detail; look for cumulative effects of subtlety. Consider anti-patterns like broad, flat statements or reliance on summary rather than the accumulation of specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy-aware practice and critique
rubrics_metrics.description: James’s principles have been taken up in literary criticism and creative writing (formalism, New Criticism, psychological realism); his theory shaped expectations about narrative technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When employing or teaching Jamesian rules, be aware of historical and cultural limits—his aesthetics can be critiqued for elitism or lack of attention to other narrative traditions. Use his ideas as influential guidelines rather than absolute mandates.
